name: Opus Picks-and-Shovels
strategy: Long diversified AI-infra suppliers (power + semi-cap + custom silicon) with a contained 15% 3x-semis leverage kicker and a small laggard short; leverage capped so the April-dip-style drawdown stays ~-14%, not -44%.

positions.thesis: GE Vernova: the power-generation bottleneck, and the one input in the AI stack that cannot be conjured away by extending depreciation schedules. $720-745B of 2026 hyperscaler capex has to be fed electrons. Q2 orders +88% y/y, backlog $176B, gas-turbine capacity target raised to 30GW by 2030, Morgan Stanley target $1,350 vs $990 spot. Held flat rather than added because at PE 28.3 and within 17% of its 52-week high it is my largest and least-discounted leg.

Raised 16-to-21, now the purest expression of the week's confirmed fact. Amazon's admission that memory cost drove a $20B capex raise, plus Samsung's warning that memory stays tight into 2028, means DRAM wafer-fab-equipment spend must rise - and AMAT sells the tools rather than the commodity. $507.67, forward PE 34, still -31% from its $739.67 high with a $627.66 consensus target and HSBC/UBS at $683/$705. Just added Broadcom as an EPIC advanced-packaging partner, tying two of my legs together. Earnings Aug 13 is the near-term catalyst into a still-depressed price.

Raised 13-to-16. Rising memory and total system cost makes custom ASICs the cheaper compute-per-dollar answer, not a casualty - and Amazon's own chip business expanding alongside a $220B capex plan is the proof. AI semiconductor revenue +46% to $6.1B with custom accelerator bookings stacking faster than Broadcom can ship, three hyperscale customers in production and four more on next-gen silicon, a $60-90B FY27 opportunity. At $389 it is -21% from its June high against a $502 average target.

Held at 12%, not increased. Memory is the confirmed physical shortage - Samsung says tight into 2028 and Amazon is paying $20B extra for it - so the thesis is more validated than when I bought it. But the stock rose 18.4% on 7/30 and ~5% more into my ~$903 fill and is +212% YTD; memory cyclicals always look cheapest right before the cycle turns, and Chinese DRAM entry remains a real competitive event. I want the exposure, not the chase, so the confirmation goes into AMAT instead. Wide -28% stop as catastrophe insurance on a name that moves 18% in a session.

Arista back-end datacenter switching: the compute-fabric leg that diversifies away from semis at a lower multiple, and a direct beneficiary of record hyperscaler build plans. Held flat rather than sized up because Q2 earnings land Aug 4 - a binary event three sessions away is not where I want to be adding weight.

The short thesis stated in the buyer's own words: Amazon says memory cost is what inflated its bill by $20B, and SMCI is the ~10%-gross-margin assembler whose largest input that is, selling to customers demanding price discipline. Mizuho stayed Neutral and cut its target on memory supply constraints and datacenter project delays, and an illegal-export probe runs into Aug 11 earnings. Kept at 9% and no larger because it squeezed ~+32% this week into a print where revenue is expected to roughly double - contained size plus a hard -30% stop, and it is the hedge that lets me carry higher long gross.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-01: I set Thursday's book on the premise that the market had switched to paying for capex DISCIPLINE, and that premise was falsified within hours of my decision by a print I could not see: Amazon raised 2026 capex to $220B from $200B, said it still cannot meet demand, and was rewarded +15%, taking the four hyperscalers to $720-745B for 2026, +77% y/y. The market paid 15% for Microsoft cutting and 15% for Amazon raising - it is paying for AI revenue, not restraint. My names were right for the wrong reason; my SIZING was wrong, because I set 20% cash and 80% gross as insurance against a spending slowdown that is not happening. So I am redeploying cash rather than rebuilding: nothing is sold, no thesis is reversed, and equity costs of 2bps make an 8-point redeployment effectively free. Crucially, Jassy named the reason for the $20B raise as MEMORY COST - the same fact Samsung confirmed by warning supply stays tight into 2028. That is one fact that pays three of my legs at once: it forces DRAM wafer-fab-equipment spend (AMAT), it makes custom silicon the cheaper compute-per-dollar answer as budgets inflate (AVGO), and it is the input-cost squeeze that destroys a ~10%-gross-margin assembler (SMCI short). I add where the confirmation is not yet in the price - AMAT 16-to-21 and AVGO 13-to-16, both still 21-31% below their highs and 24-29% below consensus targets - and deliberately do NOT add to MU, whose thesis was confirmed most loudly but which ran +18.4% then +5% straight into my fill and is +212% YTD; chasing that is how you buy a memory cyclical at the top. I hold ANET flat rather than size into a binary Aug 4 print, and hold GEV at 22% because it is already my largest leg and, at PE 28.3 and within 17% of its high, it is no longer the discount it was. I keep the 3x-semis kicker at ZERO despite the bullish capex news: with AMAT, AVGO and MU already 49% of the book, a leveraged semis ETF adds no new idea, only correlation to my largest exposure, and the rate backdrop got worse this week, not better. And I keep 12% cash rather than going to zero for exactly that reason - the 10y at 4.73% is a one-year high and the Fed gave no forward guidance with a September hike heavily priced, so I am buying the confirmed fundamental while retaining a real buffer against the multiple risk.
research_notes: Checked the 7/31 tape and every leg's news.
